name: Electric Bicycle
description: A two- or three-wheeled bicycle with fully operable pedals, a seat or saddle and an electric motor of not more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: class 1 and class 2 (throttle) stop at 20 mph, class 3 (pedal assist) at 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; class 2 can propel it without pedaling and stops at 20 mph; class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
restrictions.citation: Nevada Revised Statutes §484B.017, as amended by SB 383 (2021)

restrictions.rule: Not a moped or an electric scooter
The motor must cut out when the rider stops pedaling or when the brakes are applied
Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be tampered with or modified to change its motor's speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
No statewide minimum age or helmet requirement for any class
Carries no more people than it's designed and equipped for, and the rider must sit on its seat
Has a bicycle's rights and duties on the road, and is ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, highways, bike lanes, bicycle paths and shared-use paths
A local authority by ordinance, or a state agency after notice and a hearing, may ban it or one of its classes from a bicycle or shared-use path, for public health and safety or legal reasons
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed
State law doesn't define an electric motorcycle; the Joint Interim Standing Committee on the Judiciary began studying them in late 2025
